approachQuestion.prompt:
How many shortest deliveries? A directed graph has unit-length edges. Given s and t, return the number of distinct shortest s-to-t vertex sequences modulo 1000000007. Return 0 if t is unreachable; when s=t, the empty-edge route counts as one. Routes are distinct when their vertex sequences differ.

The read-only outgoing lists contain IDs 0..V-1, with 1 <= V <= 200000 and 0 <= E <= 400000. There are no self-loops or duplicate ordered edges. All modular additions fit in signed 64-bit integers.

Example 1: lists=[[1,2],[3],[3],[]], s=0,t=3, output=2.
Example 2: lists=[[1,2],[2],[]], s=0,t=2, output=1: [0,2] is shorter than [0,1,2].

options.text: Use BFS with distance and count arrays. Initialize s at distance zero with count one. On first discovery of v from u, set its distance to distance[u]+1 and copy count[u]. For another edge reaching v at that same distance, add count[u] modulo the modulus. Process the full BFS.
options.feedback: Shortest routes into v must come from the preceding distance layer. BFS processes every such predecessor before v propagates its final count, so ties are added without including longer walks.

options.text: Run BFS with one parent per vertex and return 1 if t is reached, otherwise 0.
options.feedback: Example 1 has two shortest routes merging at 3. Keeping a single parent proves existence but discards the second route, so it returns 1 instead of 2.

options.text: Run a queue traversal and add count[u] to count[v] for every inspected edge u->v, even if v is closer to s than u or has the same distance.
options.feedback: In lists=[[1,2],[2],[]], s=0,t=2, this adds the contribution along 0->1->2 to the direct route and reports 2. Only predecessors exactly one layer earlier belong to shortest routes.

options.text: Enumerate every simple s-to-t route, retain the minimum edge count, and count all routes of that length modulo the modulus.
options.feedback: A shortest route is simple, so this gives the right result, but enumerating routes is unnecessarily inefficient: the number of simple routes can grow exponentially. Distance-layer counts combine equivalent prefixes directly.

feedback.reason: Equal-distance rediscovery must contribute another count, while longer rediscovery must contribute nothing. A single visited bit cannot express both rules.
details: Initialize distances to -1 and counts to zero. Set distance[s]=0 and count[s]=1 and enqueue s. For each removed u, inspect every outgoing edge u->v. If v is unseen, set distance[v]=distance[u]+1, set count[v]=count[u] and enqueue v. Otherwise, add count[u] to count[v] modulo 1000000007 only when distance[v]=distance[u]+1. After the queue empties, return count[t].

Add a predecessor's count only along an edge increasing distance by exactly one. Longer or backward routes do not count. Equal-distance BFS layers ensure every shortest predecessor contributes before its child is processed.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze bfs-distance-count. V is the total vertex count and E the directed edge count (or undirected edges stored twice where specified). Use preallocated indexed arrays and a V-slot frontier, with constant-time indexing and head/tail queue or stack operations. Include array initialization and all explicitly described scans. No hashing, recursion, array shifting, amortized growth, or input-list copying is used. Exclude the read-only input and returned result; include all other storage. Choose the tightest worst-case pair. Counts are maintained modulo the fixed modulus, so arithmetic is constant time. Return only count[t], a scalar. Distance and count arrays are auxiliary, not excluded output.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard worst-case bound for the specified implementation.

options.text: O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(V(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Combine route counts per edge instead of traversing each possible route separately.
details: The option “O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space” is tight: two arrays initialize V entries, each reachable vertex enters the queue once, and every reachable directed edge causes one constant-time comparison and at most one modular addition. Both arrays and the queue use O(V). The option “O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space” omits this state. The option “O(V(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space” treats alternative routes as separate traversals, but counts combine them. The option “O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space” charges edge copies that are never constructed.
